raw_response:
I've been working this land since I was young. Quzhou soil I know well — sandy loam, not too deep, but it responds to water and fertilizer. My well gives me good irrigation, so I don't worry about drought like some others do.

**My thinking:**

My 8 mu goes to wheat-maize rotation — that's the backbone. Same land, wheat in winter, maize in summer. I've done it this way for decades. The wheat seed I'll get from the county station — the improved variety they've been pushing the last few years gives better yield than what my mother used to plant. For maize, I'll buy hybrid seed from the market like always, Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever the seed shop has. Everyone uses hybrid maize now. Without it you can't compete.

For cotton, I keep 3 mu. It's labor-intensive and my back isn't what it was, but the cash income is important. Cotton needs more spraying — bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I'll spray maybe six times through the season. It's exhausting but necessary.

Peanuts and mungbeans I keep small — 2 mu each. They're partly for household food and partly to sell. Peanuts fix some nitrogen so I don't need to fertilize as heavily. Mungbeans I plant quick after wheat harvest on a small patch and barely touch them.

Fertilizer — I apply what my neighbors apply and what has worked before. Maybe more urea for wheat and maize than the officials say we should, but light application always left me short. I use diammonium phosphate at sowing and top-dress urea later.

Tillage: after maize harvest I do rotary tillage before seeding wheat. For cotton and peanut plots I plough deeper in spring.
